name: Dogfight Knee Tap
keyCorrections: If they do not fall: you did not pull them forward enough — increase the forward pull with the underhook
If they step over your head: your head position was too low — keep your head at their shoulder level
If they sprawl on you: switch to the single leg — your underhook gives you the single leg entry
description: From dogfight, the knee tap uses underhook and head position to take the opponent down. The dogfight is the most common wrestling-up position from half guard bottom.
shortInstruction: From dogfight, circle your outside knee across their back, use the underhook to pull them forward, and tap their far knee with your free hand to take them down.
summary: The dogfight knee tap is the highest-percentage sweep from the dogfight position (underhook half guard). From dogfight, you use your underhook to pull the opponent forward while tapping their far knee with your free hand. Their forward momentum combined with the knee tap removes their base and tips them to the mat. The knee tap transitions directly to side control or front headlock.
whyItWorks: The underhook in dogfight gives you control of their upper body — you can pull them forward, off-balancing them
Tapping the far knee removes their rear base point — they cannot step back to recover balance
The combination of forward pull (underhook) and rear base removal (knee tap) creates an unsolvable balance problem
The knee tap is safe from guillotines because your head is on the outside (cheek to their shoulder)
commonMistakes: Not pulling them forward enough before tapping the knee — the knee tap alone does not cause the takedown
Tapping the near knee instead of the far knee — the near knee tap does not remove their base
Staying too low in the dogfight — stand up to create the angle for the knee tap
Releasing the underhook during the knee tap — maintain underhook control throughout
coachingCues: Pull forward, then tap the knee
Tap the far knee, not the near
safetySummary: The knee tap is a low-impact sweep — the opponent lands on their hip, not their head or neck
Do not hyperextend your knee by posting it too far across their back
If the opponent resists the knee tap by stepping back, be ready to circle to the single leg instead

systemLogic.corePrinciple: The dogfight knee tap is part of a larger dogfight system: Knee Tap → Single Leg → Re-guard

decisionTree.action: drive your inside knee to the mat and reach for their far ankle. The knee tap is your primary takedown from the dogfight position
if they post their far leg back to defend the knee tap, switch to the single leg on the posted leg. Their weight is already committed to the post
if they turn into you to defend, follow their momentum and take the back. The turn toward you exposes their back
The dogfight position is inherently unstable — commit to one option quickly rather than pausing

moneyDetails: The dogfight knee tap is the most common sweep from half guard bottom in no-gi — it works at every level
Mastering the dogfight knee tap gives you a reliable path from half guard to top position
Knee tap to side control scores 2 points (sweep) in IBJJF
fixItFast: If they do not fall: pull harder and tap the far knee again
If they step over: sprawl back and re-establish the underhook from a lower angle
If they sit back: release the underhook and recover to neutral
